title: Microstarter pricing templates and quickstart hooks for incubator devs
summary: Hands-on microcopy + pricing experiments aimed at very early startups and incubator teams. Emphasis on low friction, predictable cost language and 3-tier quickstarts (30s -> 15m -> 1hr).
content:
Context and goal:

This is a working brief for a microstarter segment: very early-stage startups, incubators, and hackathon teams who want to prototype fast and understand cost predictability. The aim is to produce short, testable pricing strings, onboarding microcopy, and quickstart templates that keep friction low while surfacing unit economics clearly.

Audience archetypes (for tailoring):
- Solo founder / prototyper (wants 30s proof-of-life, cannot risk surprise bills)
- Hacker / hackathon team (fast loop, uses free credits, needs sample prompts and rate recommendations)
- Incubator program admin (bundled credits for cohorts, wants simple all-in reporting)

Core GTM positioning pillars (developer-first translation):
1) Predictable by default — simple, transparent unit pricing and a built-in usage cap that prevents surprise charges.
2) Fast to prototype — 3-minute to 1-hour paths with runnable examples and SDK snippets.
3) Production-ready scaling — show how a prototype plugs into Redwood Dedicated later with the same API and better cost/latency.

Quickstart ladder (3 tiers to A/B test in-product and in emails):
- 30s: "Hello world" curl + one-line SDK snippet, uses free 500-token sample, CTA: "Run in your terminal".
- 15m: Minimal app recipe (chat widget + 3 sample prompts, persistent API key, suggestion to enable prefix cache) with expected cost estimate for 1k interactions.
- 1hr: Prototype-to-demo checklist (CDN + simple fallback policy to smaller model, cost projection worksheet).

Concrete pricing-language drafts (short, to test):
- "Free 1,000 tokens to get you to a working prototype — no card required. Usage stops at your cap."
- "Pay-as-you-grow: $0.80 / 1k tokens for standard models, $0.18 / 1k embedding units. Reserved pricing available for teams scaling beyond $X/month."
- "Incubator bundle: 50k credit pack (3 months) — includes priority onboarding, cohort dashboard, and an ops consult."

Alternative microcopy variants (for A/B):
- Safety-first: "Start free. We’ll never bill without confirmation — set a cap and we’ll block overtime calls."
- Velocity-first: "Prototype in under 15 minutes — sample code, ready widgets, and a cost preview before you push."
- Economy-first: "Low cost per token + automagic batching for common patterns (chat, summarization) to reduce your bill."

Sample email snippet (onboarding drip #1):
"Subject: Your Redwood prototype credits are ready
Hey {{first_name}},
Your 1,000 tokens are active — try this curl to see a response in under a second. No card, no surprises. If you like what you see, we’ll show you a 15-minute recipe to plug it into a small demo site and an expected cost for 1,000 chat messages. — Jordan, Product"

In-product microcopy for cost controls:
- Button: "Start free demo (500 tokens)"
- Tooltip: "Set a monthly cap to avoid unexpected charges; we’ll pause calls if you hit it."
- Modal copy when toggling to paid: "You’re switching to paid usage — estimated monthly cost for your current test traffic: ~$12. Confirm billing and set a hard cap."

Pricing experiment matrix (recommended initial tests):
- Test A: Free 1k tokens, no card, cap opt-in at account level. Track conversion to second-runner within 7 days.
- Test B: Free 500 tokens + 30-day $25 dev credit (card required) — measure time-to-second API call and card abandonment.
- Test C: Incubator bundle outreach (cohort reps) offering 50k credits + onboarding — measure program adoption and churn at 3 months.

Unit economics primer (short, for sales/marketing):
- Assume typical early prototype uses 400 tokens / interaction. At $0.80 / 1k tokens, each interaction costs $0.32. A 100-interaction demo = $32.
- Opportunities to lower: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, suggest smaller model variants for non-critical tasks, and automatic batching for background jobs.

Competitive positioning notes (concise):
- Competitor A focuses on model breadth but bills per-request unpredictably; message our advantage: "predictable per-token rates + caps to avoid surprises."
- Competitor B advertises ultra-low per-token price but requires complex commitments and different APIs for hosted vs. dedicated — message our advantage: "same API as you scale to Dedicated / Private."
- Competitor C has generous free-tier but throttles throughput heavily; our angle: "free credits with burst-friendly throughput and clear limits."

Example objection responses (for sales playbook):
- "Price seems high for prototyping" -> "We give a free starter pack and clear per-run cost estimates. Plus, our batching/caching tips typically reduce prototype bills by 30% without changing UX."
- "I don’t want my prototype to become a surprise bill" -> "Set a hard cap on the project; we block calls above it and proactively alert you."

Onboarding checklist for incubator admins (one-liner items):
- Provision cohort credits (50k) and assign per-team quotas.
- Share 15m starter recipe and a demo site.
- Run a 30-min cohort office hours to walk teams through billing controls and cost-reduction tips.

Metrics to track (initial 8 weeks):
- Activation: % of teams that make API call within 24h of credit grant.
- Retention: % that make a second call within 7 days.
- Cost surprise incidents: number of accounts that hit auto-block vs. require manual intervention.
- Conversion: % that attach card and move to paid usage within 30 days.

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- Should incubator bundles be time-limited credits or rolling monthly credits? Hypothesis: time-limited increases urgency and demo velocity.
- How much visibility do incubator admins need in the console? Test: cohort dashboard vs. monthly CSV.
- Would an "auto-throttle" (reduce to cheaper model when cap nears) increase conversions? Run small cohort test.

Notes to engineering/docs:
- Provide a 15-minute sample app in three languages (Node, Python, Go) that includes explicit token-count estimates in README.
- Expose an API hook to set/modify per-project hard caps via SDK (low friction) and return clear JSON usage summaries in the dashboard.

Next steps (owner: Jordan):
1) Run two microcopy A/B tests in onboarding flow this month.
2) Draft incubator bundle landing page copy and pricing ops playbook (cohort admin flow).
3) Coordinate with docs team to add token-estimate snippets to the 15m recipe.

Quick list of creative variants to produce (for design + copy sprint):
- 3 hero headlines for landing page (predictable cost, fastest onramp, same API to scale)
- 6 short microcopy CTAs (30s, 15m, 1hr)
- 2 pricing table sketches (Free -> Pay-as-you-go -> Incubator bundle)

Rough timeline: 3 weeks to run initial experiments and collect directionally valid signals.

------
Informal notes / scribbles (raw brainstorming):
- Consider "safety net" language: founders hate surprise bills. Make it our tagline for starter pack.
- Can we auto-suggest a cap on signup based on IP/examples? e.g., "Most teams in your region choose $25/mo cap"
- Hand-holded cohort onboarding increases activation by anecdotally ~20% — consider offering a 30-min pickup call for incubator cohorts.

End.
